reviews.title: Constant crashes, misleading previews and poor AI quality
reviews.text:
⭐ 1/5 – Constant Crashes, Misleading Advertising and Poor AI Production

Extremely disappointing, especially for a paid subscription.

The app crashes so frequently that I cannot watch a single episode without multiple interruptions. It’s virtually unusable.

The content behind the paywall is also noticeably lower quality than the advertised preview. The AI-generated dialogue is poorly produced, with inconsistent pronunciation of basic words and character names. In one drama, the main character, Lyra, is pronounced “Lie-rah” by her sister and “Lee-rah” by her mother. Apparently, even the characters can’t agree on each other’s names!

This isn’t just a minor technical glitch or a matter of personal taste. It’s a paid streaming service that struggles to perform its most basic function, combined with content that falls well below the quality suggested by its advertising.

Charging a subscription for such an unreliable, poorly quality-controlled experience is unacceptable.

I would strongly recommend avoiding DramaBox until the developers address the constant crashes, improve production quality and ensure their advertising accurately reflects the paid content.

reviews.title: Psychological manipulation disguised as an entertainment app
reviews.text: This app is an absolute scam disguised as a streaming service. They charge an outrageous $25 a week, which is over $100 a month, making it vastly more expensive than premium platforms like Netflix or Prime Video for low-quality, 1-minute vertical clips.The entire app is psychologically engineered to exploit and frustrate the user. They deliberately cut every 60-second episode at an abrupt, high-stakes cliffhanger, throwing up an emotional paywall right when they think you are hooked enough to impulse-pay.If you try to use the "free" option, it is completely unplayable. Forcing users to watch up to 8 highly annoying, repetitive ads just to unlock a single one-minute clip is a blatant attempt to break your patience and bully you into buying their overpriced subscriptions. They are intentionally making the app as frustrating as possible just to milk people for profit.These kinds of predatory, gamified paywall systems do not belong in entertainment apps. Save your money and do not download this garbage. It deserves a zero-star rating.

reviews.title: Great Idea Buried Under Greed
reviews.text:
The concept is genuinely addictive, which is probably the only reason this gets two stars rather than one. Unfortunately, the quality and pricing are almost laughably mismatched.

The AI-generated videos are riddled with inconsistencies. Characters can change appearance between scenes, voices and speech often sound unnatural, facial expressions don’t match what’s happening, and scenery or character behaviour can suddenly make absolutely no sense. It regularly feels like you’re watching an unfinished AI experiment rather than a paid entertainment product.

And then there’s the price. Around £20 PER WEEK is absurd for content of this quality. That’s an extraordinary amount of money for poorly generated, inconsistent AI videos. The value simply isn’t there.

The coin system makes it even worse. Having to play games, complete offers or jump through hoops to earn enough coins just to continue watching a show is ridiculous. It feels less like a streaming service and more like a system deliberately designed to frustrate you into spending more money.

There’s actually a good idea buried underneath all of this, and the stories can be entertaining enough to keep you watching. But the AI quality needs major improvement, the pricing needs a serious reality check, and the whole coin mechanic needs to be reconsidered.

reviews.title: Never got product that I paid for
reviews.text:
I purchased a large number of tokens during a 70% off sale, as there were several shows that looked interesting. Unfortunately, I never received the tokens. I reached out for support but didn’t get a response.

After waiting, I decided to cancel and request a refund through Apple, who were very helpful.

A few weeks later, I watched a Dramabox advertisement that included a few free episodes. As soon as the preview ended, I received a message saying I had been refunded after watching paid content, and that if I made another purchase, that amount would be deducted from my balance.

This felt really dishonest and confusing. It may be a glitch, but it was frustrating enough that I wouldn’t feel comfortable purchasing again. Just be cautious when buying tokens.

It’s a shame, as I would have liked the chance to properly enjoy the app.
